absence_semantics: ABSENCE_ONLY = NO_LIFECYCLE_EVENT. No existing authority (Development Plan text, taxonomy, registry, or code) permits treating 'phi absent in current run' as invalidated/expired/failed. This is directly confirmed by Step 3's own established finding and re-confirmed with fresh real-data examples in this audit's structural inspection (see below): the SAME real causal claim (ai_capex -> gpu_demand for NVDA) disappears from Alpha Memory's view in several real runs (1496aac6, 40bd7e3d, 6f4e07f9, e434f80b) purely because its alpha_ids linkage was empty in those runs' Structure Graphs -- not because the underlying claim or thesis changed. Absence remains, by default, semantically empty.

structural_inspection_of_real_artifacts.method: Qualitative inspection of already-persisted NVDA structure_graph.json files across many real runs, using this session's own already-computed instability-signal diagnostics (Step 2/3) -- no LLM/Provider judgment used.

cases.case: ai_capex -> causal -> gpu_demand: alpha_ids empty in 4 real runs (1496aac6, 40bd7e3d, 6f4e07f9, e434f80b), alpha_ids=['A101'] in 3 others, alpha_ids=['A101','A103'] in 3 others
cases.superficial_appearance: Could look like 'A101's supporting structure was invalidated' in the 4 empty-alpha_ids runs.
cases.actual_cause: Pipeline-internal Alpha-linkage variance (already documented in the ablation audit's alpha-attribution-instability finding) -- the causal claim itself persisted; only the automated Alpha-attribution step's output differed run to run.
cases.why_not: No authority distinguishes 'linkage noise' from 'genuine thesis change' at this signal alone; treating it as invalidation would produce false positives on every run affected by ordinary attribution variance.

cases.case: ai_capex -> [causal | supportive] -> nvda_revenue_growth: edge_type flips between 'causal' and 'supportive' across different real runs for the identical node pair
cases.superficial_appearance: Could look like 'the causal claim weakened to a merely supportive one' -- a plausible-sounding thesis softening.
cases.actual_cause: Independent LLM canonical-relation-type extraction variance (already documented in the ablation audit) -- the underlying evidence text driving this classification was not shown to differ meaningfully between these runs.
cases.why_not: Cannot be distinguished, using only currently persisted structured fields, from ordinary extraction noise; doing so would require re-reading and comparing the underlying claim TEXT with a new semantic judgment, which is out of scope for this step and not yet authorized.

cases.case: ai_capex -> supportive -> nvda_revenue_growth: alpha attribution varies across FOUR different variants (none / A101 / A101+A103 / A103) across real runs
cases.superficial_appearance: Could look like 'A103's supporting structure appeared and disappeared repeatedly' -- a volatile/unstable thesis.
cases.actual_cause: Same Alpha-linkage variance as case 1 -- confirmed by cross-referencing against the SAME node pair's behavior in the other edge_type variant.

structural_inspection_of_real_artifacts.overall_conclusion: In every real case inspected, what might superficially look like invalidation, disappearance, or thesis reversal is fully and satisfactorily explained by already-documented pipeline extraction/attribution variance (Steps 1.5/1.6's own findings) -- not by any genuine, evidenced change in the underlying research claim. This directly and concretely supports keeping ABSENCE_ONLY = NO_LIFECYCLE_EVENT as the default.

recommended_minimum_model_reasoning: MODEL 1 (explicit taxonomy invalidation conditions that are deterministically machine-evaluable) requires at least ONE condition to be EXECUTABLE_NOW_DETERMINISTIC or EXECUTABLE_FROM_EXISTING_STRUCTURED_OUTPUT -- the audit found ZERO such conditions among all 30 enumerated (0 in either category; see invalidation_condition_count_summary). There is therefore no non-empty MODEL 1 to implement today. MODEL 2 (invalidation + purely observational recurrence-derived events) is also not reachable: Section D's own analysis found no candidate signal classified AUTHORIZED_INVALIDATION_SIGNAL-and-executable (the one AUTHORIZED signal, A101's taxonomy conditions, is authorized as CONTENT but not as an EXECUTABLE RULE). MODEL 0 (no lifecycle events can be operationalized yet) is therefore the narrowest defensible choice, and the correct one -- not a failure of this audit, but its honest conclusion. Steps 1-3's already-shipped, purely observational recurrence/history layer remains fully valid and useful on its own; it is simply not yet 'lifecycle' in the invalidation/expiry/failure sense the Plan names.
authorized_events_note: No event is authorized for implementation at this time (MODEL 0). If Product later authorizes specific content (e.g. approves machine-evaluable invalidation conditions for more Alphas, or defines an expiry window), the EVENT FACT vs EVENT INTERPRETATION separation below should govern the eventual spec: a fact (e.g. 'ticker-specific evidence count = 0') must never automatically become an interpretation (e.g. 'phi invalidated') without an explicit, Product-approved rule connecting them -- exactly the failure mode this audit was designed to prevent.
persistence_recommendation: BOTH, conditionally, once any event is ever authorized -- but as A first (recompute from persisted source runs) as the default, with B (durable immutable event persistence) added ONLY where recomputation cost or a genuine audit-immutability requirement justifies it. Reasoning: (1) auditability favors recomputation, since the source-of-truth runs are already the audit trail Steps 1-3 rely on; (2) deterministic replay is trivially guaranteed by recomputation (unchanged inputs -> unchanged outputs), which durable persistence does not automatically guarantee unless carefully versioned; (3) taxonomy/version changes are handled cleanly by recomputation (a version bump changes the computed identity/result automatically) but would require an explicit migration/reclassification policy for durably-persisted events; (4) corrected historical data and human review are easier to reconcile against a recompute-from-source model (fix the source, recompute) than against durably-persisted events that would need explicit retraction/supersession semantics; (5) event reclassification (Product later redefining what an event means) is trivial under recomputation (redeploy the new rule, recompute) but requires a migration under durable persistence. Recommendation: default to recompute-only (A), matching this codebase's own established pattern (Steps 1-3's phi/recurrence/aggregate/instability-signal layers are ALL already recompute-only, no new table). Durable persistence (B) should be considered later, specifically and narrowly, ONLY if/when a genuine performance problem is measured -- never introduced speculatively. NO DB TABLE IS RECOMMENDED NOW.
